newsitem.title: UK: Oil industry demand backs UK-Algeria cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: Oil industry demand backs UK-Algeria cargo flights.

text.p: Bouyant demand for oil industry equipment is supporting a weekly Boeing 737QC (quick-change) freighter service between London Luton airport and the Hassi Messaoud oilfield in Algeria, an air cargo industry source told Reuters.

The plane is chartered from Air Algerie by customs clearance agent and general shipping forwarder, Algerie Forage Service Express (AFSE), based in Hassi Messaoud, with the charter paid for in Algerian dinars.

The plane offers 11 tonnes of capacity for all-palletised freight and flies oil-industry related equipment coming from a wide range of countries, including the U.S. (Houston), France and Germany, an executive from the UK handling agent, Daher (UK) Ltd said.

The change to cargo from passenger configuration is carried out at Algiers and the plane then leaves empty for Luton where it lands at midnight on Wednesdays before departing for Hassi Messaoud two hours later, he added.
"And with the aircraft operating in all-cargo capacity, we can carry hazardous goods, which would not be allowed on passsenger or combi flights," he added.
"If we require extra capacity, we would look at chartering a Lockheed Hercules, which does have the advantage of a rear-loading door. In fact we have already had several Hercules charters," he added.
"We see this service continuing for quite a few years, given the long-term expansion plans for Algerian oil," he said
